document.title: Comments of Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Inc. re PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.’s Reliability Backstop Procurement filing

pages.text:
1 
 
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
 
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                               ) 
Docket No. ER26-3380-000 
 
COMMENTS OF SOUTHERN MARYLAND ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC. 
 
Pursuant to the Combined Notice of Filings #1 issued by the Federal Energy Regulatory 
Commission (“Commission”) on August 3, 2026, Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative, Inc. 
(“SMECO”)1 respectfully submits these comments regarding the filing that PJM Interconnection, 
L.L.C. (“PJM”) submitted in the above-captioned docket on July 31, 2026 (the “RBP Filing”).2  
PJM proposes revisions to the PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”) and the 
Reliability Assurance Agreement Among Load Serving Entities (“RAA”) to establish a one-time 
“Reliability Backstop Procurement” (“RBP”) of new capacity, the costs of which PJM proposes 
to recover through a new charge (the “RBP Charge”) assessed against a subset of Load Serving 
Entities (“LSEs”) in the PJM Region.    
SMECO acknowledges that additional capacity is needed to address the shortfall reflected 
in the 2028/2029 Delivery Year (“DY”) Base Residual Auction (“BRA”) and PJM's decision to 
pursue that capacity through a one-time backstop mechanism, the RBP.   SMECO’s comments 
focus on the roles the RBP Filing assigns to Electric Distributors in making those determinations, 
and certain aspects of the RBP credit and collateral requirements proposed in the RBP Filing.  
 
1 On August 4, 2026,SMECO submitted, and the Commission accepted, a (Doc-less) Motion to Intervene in this 
proceeding: https://elibrary.ferc.gov/eLibrary/filedownload?fileid=857BC7F7-7CD8-CD58-9E7A-9FCDA3B00000  
2Reliability Backstop Procurement to Address Resource Adequacy Concerns Stemming from Large Loads, 
Transmittal Letter of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Docket No. ER26-3380-000 (July 31, 2026) (“RBP Filing”):

2 
 
I. INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY  
PJM's RBP proposal responds to an actual reliability concern – namely, that the 2028/2029 
DY BRA cleared 6,831.3 MW short of the PJM Region Reliability Requirement.  This shortfall, 
as PJM notes, was driven in part by the rapid interconnection of large loads, including data 
centers.3  SMECO agrees that this shortfall must be addressed.   
However, SMECO has comments in two areas.  First, PJM’s proposal assigns Electric 
Distributors a series of functions that exceed the metering and data-reporting functions Electric 
Distributors have historically performed for PJM under the PJM Operating Agreement (“OA”). 
Second, as to RBP credit, PJM proposes vastly different RBP collateral requirements as  
between RBP load versus RBP supply. SMECO serves a service territory that has attracted data 
center interest, and as such, has an interest in seeing a rational PJM RBP credit policy established.  
II. BACKGROUND 
PJM filed the RBP Filing on July 31, 2026, requesting that the Commission act by 
September 29, 2026 -- sixty days after filing -- so that PJM may commence the RBP on September 
30, 2026.4  PJM proposes to set an “Initial RBP Target” equal to the 6,831.3 MW UCAP shortfall 
reflected in the 2028/2029 DY BRA (excluding Fixed Resource Requirement load and supply), 
and to decrement that Initial RBP Target by two categories of MWs to arrive at a “Final RBP 
Target”: (1) “Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW,” meaning new capacity, matched with new load, 
that PJM verifies was not previously counted as either an RPM commitment or an FRR resource; 
and (2) “Opt-Out UCAP MW,” a narrow opt-out available in limited circumstances.5 PJM 
proposes to procure that Final RBP Target quantity through the RBP. 
 
3RBP Filing at 21 (“6,831.3 MW UCAP”); see also id. at 1 (describing the shortfall as “primarily driven by the 
unprecedented addition of large loads, most notably data centers”). 
4RBP Filing at 3, Footnote 5 and at 27. 
5RBP Filing at 31, 35, 44 (proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, sections 18.1, 18.2).

3 
 
PJM proposes to allocate the resulting daily RBP Charges first to Electric Distributor 
zones/areas, pro rata, based on each zone/area's share of the region-wide Final RBP Target -- = 
adjusted to reflect zone-specific Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW.6  Within each zone/area, PJM 
proposes that cost allocation to individual LSEs “be based on ‘the state and/or RERRA-determined 
allocation of cleared RBP UCAP MW to LSEs within each Electric Distributor's zone/area, as 
reported [to PJM] by each Electric Distributor.’”7    
This state/RERRA-determined allocation is referred to as the “RBP Obligation” or 
“RBO.”8  LSEs allocated RBP cost responsibility -- an RBO -- must post collateral (“RBP 
Collateral”) in an amount equal to a uniform “RBP Credit Rate” -- proposed by PJM to be at $1.5 
million per MW -- multiplied by the LSE's allocated RBP UCAP MW.9  An LSE with an RBO 
must post this RBP Collateral no later than forty-five days before the start of the relevant DY -- 
just fifteen days after the underlying RBO allocation on which the collateral requirement depends 
is reported (i.e., the RBO must be reported no later than sixty days before the DY).10 
 
III. COMMENTS 
A.  
PJM’s RBP Filing Assigns Electric Distributors a Role Inconsistent with Their 
Intended Function in PJM 
The term “Electric Distributor” refers to a Member “sector” under the PJM OA, defined 
principally by reference to a Member's ownership or lease of distribution facilities serving load in 
the PJM Region, including cooperative and joint municipal systems.11  Historically, the functions 
Electric Distributors perform for PJM under the OA and RAA have centered on metering and load-
 
6RBP Filing at 96-97 (proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(a)). 
7RBP Filing at 97-98 (quoting proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3(b)(iii)). 
8RBP Filing at 98 (quoting proposed Tariff, Definitions -- RBP Obligation). 
9RBP Filing at 114-118 (proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(b)). 
10RBP Filing at 120. 
11See generally OA, Definitions -- Electric Distributor.

4 
 
data reporting -- classic “meter reading” roles such as reporting hourly net energy flows for 
settlement purposes.12  Even OA section 11.3.3 (h), which requires that an Electric Distributor 
“[p]rovide to the Office of the Interconnection all System, accounting, customer tracking, load 
forecasting (including all load to be served from its System) and other data necessary or 
appropriate to implement or administer this Agreement, and the Reliability Assurance Agreement” 
does not result in an Electric Distributor performing the following  expansive set of Tasks: 
1. 
Sponsor of reductions to the zone's RBP target (opt-outs)13: Electric 
Distributors serve as the applicant and evidentiary sponsor -- the opt-out 
request itself must come from the Electric Distributor, with supporting 
documentation. 
2. 
Reporting capacity offsets: Electric Distributors, along with other entities, 
provide evidentiary support for Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW claimed 
within their zone/area, which is capped at that zone/area's Load Adjustment 
amount of summer 2028 demand.14 That is, Electric Distributors must 
provide reports and evidence of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW in each 
of their respective zones/areas.15  
3. 
Bridge between state decisions, LSEs, and PJM: Electric Distributors 
must report the state/RERRA-determined allocation (i.e., the RBO)16; 
absent a report, PJM falls back to a Peak Load Contribution share of Daily 
Unforced Capacity Obligation. 
4. 
RBO Cost allocation: Electric Distributors' reports feed both the zone-
level allocation of the Final RBP Target and the LSE-level daily formula17, 
with PJMSettlement as the Counterparty responsible for collecting from 
LSEs.18 
5. 
Supporting DER and Demand Resource participation: Electric 
Distributors must develop and provide distribution-impact studies for RBP 
 
12See, e.g., OA, Schedule 1, section 3.6 (Metering Reconciliation); PJM Manual 28: Operating Agreement Accounting 
(describing the role of “fully metered” Electric Distribution Companies in reporting hourly net energy flows for 
settlement purposes). 
13 RBP Filing at 33, 44-46, Section III.B.3 "Opt-out".  
14 RBP Filing at 42-43; Section III.B.2.e: "Electric Distributors and other entities provide evidentiary support for 
Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW".  The RBP Filing at 32 indicates that the cap is set at the Load Adjustment for 
each Electric Distributor zone/area amount of summer 2028 demand. 
15 RBP Filing at 42-43, emphasis added, footnotes omitted. 
16 RBP Filing at 97-99, 
17 RBP Filing at 96-99.. 
18 RBP Filing at footnote 236.

5 
 
DER Aggregation Resources.19 An RBP DER Capacity Aggregation 
Resource 
must 
address 
“applicable 
Electric 
Distributor 
interconnection/distribution impact study requirements,” and an RBP 
Demand Resource must satisfy “Electric Distributor coordination 
requirements for metering, telemetry, and baseline measurement 
infrastructure.”20 
6. 
Supplying inputs that affect LSE collateral: under the Tariff provision 
for "Determining an LSE's RBP credit requirement," the Electric 
Distributor's RBO report -- as submitted, and scaled if it does not sum to the 
zone/area's Final RBP Target -- sets an LSE's RBP UCAP MW; absent an 
RBO, PJM instead uses each LSE's pro-rata share of the zone/area's Daily 
Unforced Capacity Obligation.21 
For example, with regards to RBO Cost allocation “Task #4”, the RBP Filing asks Electric 
Distributors to report “the state and/or RERRA-determined allocation of RBP UCAP MW to 
[LSEs] within each Electric Distributor’s zone/area” --  i.e., the RBO.22  But the RBO an Electric 
Distributor reports is not a metered quantity; rather, it is a state or RERRA’s own determination 
of which customers are “large loads”23, for which the Electric Distributor must “certify” to PJM, 
fixing how much each LSE in the zone will be assessed the RBP Charge.   
Neither PJM’s Filing nor the OA, so far as SMECO is aware, gives an Electric Distributor 
this role: OA section 11.324 sets forth data-reporting and other operational obligations for Electric 
 
19 RBP Filing at 75; footnote 199. 
20RBP Filing at 75 (quoting proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.5(f)(i)(12)-(13)). 
21RBP Filing at 118-119.  
22RBP Filing at 97-98. 
23RBP Filing at 98. 
24 OA 11.3.3 Electric Distributors. In addition to any of the foregoing responsibilities that may be applicable, each 
Member that is an Electric Distributor, whether or not that Member votes in the Members Committee in the Electric 
Distributor sector or meets the eligibility requirements for any other sector of the Members Committee, shall:  
(a) Accept, comply with or be compatible with all standards applicable within the PJM Region with respect to system 
design, equipment ratings, operating practices and maintenance practices as set forth in the PJM Manuals, or be subject 
to an interconnected Member’s requirements relating to the foregoing, so that sufficient electrical equipment, control 
capability, information and communication are available to the Office of the Interconnection for planning and 
operation of the PJM Region;  
(b) Assure the continued compatibility of its local system energy management system monitoring and 
telecommunications systems to satisfy the technical requirements of interacting automatically or manually with the 
Office of the Interconnection as it directs the operation of the PJM Region;  
(c) Maintain or arrange for a portion of its connected load to be subject to control by automatic underfrequency, under-
voltage, or other load-shedding devices at least equal to the levels established pursuant to the Reliability Assurance 
Agreement, or be subject to another Member’s control for these purposes;

6 
 
Distributor Members, but it does not contemplate a Member determining or certifying to PJM an 
allocation of a FERC-jurisdictional “RBP Charge” among other Members’ customers, including 
helping assemble the “sufficient evidence” PJM requires to support any Qualifying RBP Offset 
UCAP MW claimed within its zone/area.25  These tasks become harder still where it is the LSE, 
not the Electric Distributor, that holds the underlying large-load data. 
Regarding Electric Distributor “Task #5” from the list above, PJM’s RBP Filing requires 
that the RBP DER Aggregation or Demand Resource seller demonstrate it has coordinated with 
the Electric Distributor to meet requirements.26 The RBP Filing itself never defines these 
requirements; the Electric Distributor is thus placed in a gatekeeper role over how these types of 
capacity resources can submit an RBP Sell Offer; presumably this is as soon as September 30, 
2026 – the earliest planned opening date of the RBP sell-offer window.  But this function also 
 
(d) Provide or arrange for sufficient reactive capability and voltage control facilities to conform to Good Utility 
Practice and (i) to meet the reactive requirements of its system and customers and (ii) to maintain adequate voltage 
levels and the stability required by the bulk power supply facilities of the PJM Region;  
(e) Shed connected load, share Generation Capacity Resources and take such other coordination actions as may be 
necessary in accordance with the directions of the Office of the Interconnection in Emergencies;  
(f) Maintain or arrange for a portion of its Generation Capacity Resources at least equal to the level established 
pursuant to the Reliability Assurance Agreement to have the ability to go from a shutdown condition to an operating 
condition and start delivering power without assistance from the power system;  
(g) Provide or arrange through another Member for the services of a 24-hour local control center to coordinate with 
the Office of the Interconnection, each such control center to be furnished with appropriate telemetry equipment as 
specified in the PJM Manuals, and to be staffed by system operators trained and delegated sufficient authority to take 
any action necessary to assure that the system for which the operator is responsible is operated in a stable and reliable 
manner.  In addition to meeting any training standards and requirements specified in this Agreement, local control 
center staff shall be required to meet applicable training standards and requirements in PJM Manual 40, Control Center 
Requirements, including the PJM System Operator Training Requirements in Attachment C;  
(h) Provide to the Office of the Interconnection all System, accounting, customer tracking, load forecasting (including 
all load to be served from its System) and other data necessary or appropriate to implement or administer this 
Agreement, and the Reliability Assurance Agreement; and (i) Comply with the underfrequency relay obligations and 
charges specified in Operating Agreement, Schedule 7. 
25RBP Filing at 97: “Cost responsibility allocated to a zone/area may be further adjusted where PJM receives sufficient 
evidence demonstrating that new capacity has been brought by load to the relevant Electric Distributor’s zone/area in 
the form of Qualifying RBP Offset UCAP MW. A zone/area of an Electric Distributor that qualifies for one of the 
opt-outs set forth in proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.1(d), would also have RBP Charges reduced by the 
MW quantity of the opt-out.” (citing proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.2(c)). 
26RBP Filing at 75: “the seller must demonstrate that it has coordinated with the Electric Distributor to ensure the 
resource will meet applicable requirements” (citing proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.5(f)(i)(11)-(12)).

7 
 
conflicts with the “metering and reporting role” that OA section 11.3 assigns to Electric 
Distributors.  
B. RBP Credit and Collateral Issues.  
PJM’s proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8 imposes a credit requirement on 
LSEs.  Per the Affidavit of PJM witness Danielle Croop27, PJM's proposed initial allocation of 
RBP UCAP MW to each Electric Distributor zone/area is based on the Load Adjustments in PJM 
Table B9b of the 2026 PJM Load Forecast, applied against the region-wide Initial RBP Target of 
6,831.3 MW. 28    PJM proposes an RBP LSE Credit Rate "initially at $1.5 million" per MW.29 
Applied to the 6,831.3 MW of RBP target capacity, approximately $10.25 billion (6,831.3 MW × 
$1,500,000/MW = $10,246,950,000) would need to be posted by LSEs as collateral no later than 
45 days ahead of the start of the 2028/2029 Delivery Year. PJM derived the $1.5 million buy-side 
credit requirement as a full 15-year, $555 MW-day contract payment (discounted at 9.5%), 
yielding an RBP LSE required posting  ~ 7.5 years equivalent buy-side collateral.    
PJM proposes that the Electric Distributor’s RBO allocation be reported at no later than 
sixty days before the start of the DY; PJM proposes to require the affected LSE to post the resulting 
collateral just fifteen days later, at forty-five days before the DY begins.30  That leaves just a 
fifteen-day window to arrange collateral for an obligation whose amount it could not have 
predicted in advance, using a $1.5 million/MW RBP Credit Rate”31   Thus, once an LSE knows 
the outcome of the state/RERRA reporting process administered by the Electric Distributor, but it 
then only has two weeks to post significant RPM buy-side collateral. 
 
27 Affidavit Danielle Croop, PJM at page 12 (paragraph 46) (“Croop Affidavit”).  
28 Croop Affidavit at paragraph 4. 
29 RBP Filing at 116-117; proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, § 18.8(b)(i)(A). 
30RBP Filing at 120. 
31RBP Filing at 116 (quoting proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(b)(i)(A)).

8 
 
If the Electric Distributor uploads RBP Obligation MW for the LSEs in its zone/area that 
do not sum to the zone’s fixed Final RBP Target MW, per the RBP Filing PJM simply scales up 
each reported MW-value – and individual LSE collateral obligations – to fit the fixed Final RBP 
Target MW.32 And if the Electric Distributor reports no RBO at all for its zone/area, PJM instead 
calculates the LSE’s RBP Collateral using the LSE’s pro-rata share of the zone/area’s Daily 
Unforced Capacity Obligation, a value tied to historical peak load rather than any state/RERRA 
determination.33  At the same time, on the sell-side RBP resources have a three (3)-year, and only 
20% * RBP price of $555 MW-day collateral, posting requirement equal to $101,647/MW 
discounted at PJM’s 9.5% discount rate.  As such, RBP LSEs have a 14.5x collateral posting 
requirement of RBP supply resources.   
Moreover, if an RBP-procured generator fails to deliver or is delayed, the RBP load it 
serves is exposed to higher risk of load curtailment.  An RBP load that wants to hedge that risk by 
buying replacement capacity cannot do so,  practically speaking; a 20% shortfall penalty times 
$555 MW-day is only $111 MW-day, which is insufficient compensation to purchase new 
capacity.  Further, if an RBP resource misses its commercial operation date (“COD”) because of 
network-upgrade delays are excused from shortfall penalty charges -- no RBP shortfall charge is 
collected to compensate the load sitting exposed to “IRAS” or other elevated curtailment risk in 
the meantime.34   
 
 
32RBP Filing at 119. “For LSEs serving load in an Electric Distributor zone/area in which RBOs have been reported, 
the LSE will be required to post RBP Collateral for its RBO MW (i.e., its allocated RBP UCAP MW amount). 
Consistent with the proposed cost allocation rules, PJM proposes that “the RBP Obligation MW [will] equal[] the 
RBP Obligation MW submitted for the Load Serving Entity by the Electric Distributor and scaled, as necessary, in 
the event that the RBP Obligation MW values uploaded by the Electric Distributor do not sum to the fixed, Final RBP 
Target MW for the zone/area” (footnotes omitted). 
33Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.8(b)(i)(B)(1) 
34 See: https://www.pjm.com/-/media/DotCom/committees-groups/cifp-rbp/2026/20260610/20260610-item-03h---
smeco-presentation.pdf

9 
 
IV. CONCLUSION 
SMECO respectfully requests that the Commission consider SMECO’s comments on 
PJM’s RBP Filing.
